transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-29 15:00 PDT | Duration: 52m
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (BridgePoint - NetOps), Aisha Rahman (BridgePoint - Platform Eng), Daniel Hsu (BridgePoint - CTO)

Summary:
Weekly POC sync focused on network routing behavior, telemetry ingestion, and the planned kernel/quantization upgrade. Discussed fallback routing, MTU mismatches, KMS integration, and a short canary window for the kernel image. Agreed on action items to exchange docs and set a canary date.

Topics:
- Observed latency spikes and correlation to inter-region egress at 4pm PT
- Kernel upgrade compatibility (2.3.0 -> 2.3.1) and quantized model test plan
- Telemetry pipeline: Splunk vs Datadog ingestion, retention, and sample rate
- Fallback routing and circuit-breaker thresholds
- Compliance: SOC2, KMS/HSM integration, audit logs and RBAC

Action items (captured above): see action_items field for owners/due dates.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samira Patel: Hey everyone thanks for joining. We're at our weekly BridgePoint pilot sync. Quick roll call, and then Diego will walk through the kernel image and telemetry plan.
[00:22] Marcus Lee: yep Marcus here, NetOps. we had that late spike on thurs, i pulled logs, looks like a burst of egress to us-west-2 and then a bunch of retransmits.
[00:35] Diego Ramos: ok so on the replay i saw, there's a small chance it was MTU related, we saw IP fragments and a slow path in the runtime. our upgrade includes mtu auto-tuning in the kernel path.
[01:05] Aisha Rahman: quick Q — will that change require firewall rule changes? our egress ACLs are pretty strict, we don't want to open wide.
[01:18] Samira Patel: good call. short answer: no, not opening new ports, it's walker at the network layer, but Marcus should share the ACL set so we can validate.
[01:30] Marcus Lee: i'll drop the ACL and sample pcap in the shared drive after this. i want to flag that our security team cares about KMS and where keys are stored.
[01:45] Daniel Hsu: yeah, keys are a big one — we can't have plaintext or unmanaged key material leaving the VPC.
[01:52] Diego Ramos: understood. Redwood supports external KMS/HSM via customer-managed keys; we'll send the integration guide. there's a small caveat with our telemetry exporter if it's doing TLS termination, but we can configure mTLS and not touch key material.
[02:20] Samira Patel: action: we'll share SOC2 extracts and the KMS integration doc after the call.
[02:33] Marcus Lee: perfect.
[02:40] Diego Ramos: on the kernel upgrade itself, big picture: 2.3.1 fixes a race in KV cache eviction and improves attention kernel scheduling for short sequences. We expect a slight up tick in throughput and lower tail latency in our lab runs, but we need to validate against BridgePoint's traffic.
[03:10] Marcus Lee: what about quantized model support? our inference nodes are on Ampere A1 and we were planning int8 trials.
[03:22] Diego Ramos: int8 is supported but we have a compatibility matrix — quantized kernels use different GEMM paths. we'll run a short latency burn with quantized weights in the canary. if we see regression we'll fallback to fp16 variant.
[03:50] Daniel Hsu: fallback is critical. can we automate fallback per route or is it whole-cluster?
[03:58] Diego Ramos: we support routing at multiple levels: per-route policy, model-variant fallback, and region fallback. for this pilot we'd prefer per-route so we can isolate regression to a small set of requests.
[04:25] Aisha Rahman: how's telemetry handled? we currently ship to internal splunk and a mirror to datadog.
[04:33] Samira Patel: Redwood can stream per-request traces and token timing to your Splunk endpoint. we'll want an ingestion credential and sample rate config. default is 10% but we can tune.
[04:52] Marcus Lee: 10% is ok to start, but we need retention info — how long you keep logs on-host before expiring?
[05:02] Diego Ramos: by default platform keeps 7 days of verbose traces locally and pushes aggregates to long-term storage per your retention policy. with private deployment you control retention and we can configure log rotation and compression.
[05:20] Marcus Lee: ok good. also curious about telemetry costs, egress to Splunk, can that be batched?
[05:29] Diego Ramos: yes, batching and compression happen client-side; there's an explicit config in the runtime. that will reduce per-event egress significantly.
[05:40] Aisha Rahman: any known compatibility issues with our current on-prem network stack? we run BGP with MPLS and some overlay.
[05:50] Diego Ramos: we tested with common overlays; the main gotchas are MTU mismatches and path MTU black hole. we added an MTU auto-negotiation step in 2.3.1. still want to validate with your pcap.
[06:10] Samira Patel: can we shift a bit — timeline for canary? we suggested Nov 5-6 as a tentative window. Marcus does that work?
[06:18] Marcus Lee: Nov 5 is ok, but we prefer Nov 6 due to a maintenance window on Nov 4. need internal ok from change board.
[06:30] Daniel Hsu: i'll try to lock Nov 6; the change freeze is a blocker otherwise.
[06:37] Samira Patel: note captured: Daniel will confirm change freeze by Nov 4.
[06:45] Diego Ramos: technical details for the canary: we'll push kernel 2.3.1 to 10% of nodes, enable quantized model variant on a single route, and run a 1-hour burn at expected concurrency. we'll collect latency histograms, p99/p999, token breakdowns, and KV cache miss rates.
[07:15] Marcus Lee: do you have a bench harness or do we need to spin up our own traffic generator?
[07:22] Diego Ramos: Redwood can provide a traffic replay harness and a sample workload runner. better if we have production sample, but we'll fake-it with replay if needed.
[07:40] Aisha Rahman: on the security side, who gets access to the logs? we need RBAC.
[07:47] Samira Patel: we support SSO/SAML and role-based access; you can map groups to read-only vs admin. logs can be forwarded to your Splunk so central security team keeps custody.
[08:05] Marcus Lee: also want a runbook for rollback. what does rollback look like?
[08:12] Diego Ramos: rollback is an orchestration-driven image roll back per node; we can script an emergency fallback which will route traffic to the FP16 variant and halt canary. usual warm-up time is 30–90 seconds for cache warming.
[08:35] Daniel Hsu: 30–90s is acceptable but we need to see the runbook.
[08:40] Samira Patel: we'll publish a canary runbook with exact commands and emergency contacts.
[08:48] (crosstalk) Marcus Lee: can you also include the network validation checklist?
[08:52] Samira Patel: yes.
[09:00] Diego Ramos: quick note on fallback thresholds: we recommend circuit-breaker at 25% latency increase or 5x error rate for 2 continuous minutes. those are configurable.
[09:18] Aisha Rahman: sounds reasonable. who tunes those in prod?
[09:22] Diego Ramos: BridgePoint will own production thresholds, Redwood will help with initial recommendations during pilot.
[09:30] Marcus Lee: competitor question — is OtherInferenceCo's on-prem offering different in how they handle KV cache? they had lower p99 but worse throughput historically.
[09:42] Diego Ramos: OtherInferenceCo uses a monolithic cache with less aggressive eviction; that helps p99 at low load but degrades at scale. our approach leans on continuous batching plus smarter eviction which helps throughput.
[09:58] Daniel Hsu: ok good note.
[10:05] Samira Patel: any blockers on scheduling the canary?
[10:10] Marcus Lee: only the change board approval and me dropping the ACL/pcap. i'll get those by 11/02.
[10:18] Samira Patel: great. Diego, you'll prepare the image and bench.
[10:22] Diego Ramos: yes, prepping the 2.3.1 image, quantized model build, bench harness and an automated results sheet.
[10:32] (brief pause)
[10:48] Marcus Lee: side note — telemetry volume might hit egress cap for the month, any suggestions?
[10:54] Diego Ramos: lower sample rate during burn-in, batch, and compress; we can also stream only aggregates during high volume windows.
[11:10] Aisha Rahman: what about encryption in transit?
[11:14] Samira Patel: mTLS between nodes and to Splunk; keys remain in your KMS, Redwood never sees plaintext keys.
[11:25] Daniel Hsu: that's the requirement.
[11:30] Samira Patel: ok, wrapping. Quick recap and next steps.
[11:35] Diego Ramos: i'll circulate the canary checklist and bench plan.
[11:38] Samira Patel: i'll send SOC2 extracts, KMS doc, and the runbook stub. Marcus will share ACLs/pcap and Daniel will confirm change freeze. we'll aim for Nov 6 canary.
[11:50] Marcus Lee: confirmed i'll do the ACL and pcap by 11/02.
[11:56] Daniel Hsu: i'll update by 11/04.
[12:02] Samira Patel: thanks all, we'll follow up with invites for a pre-canary walkthrough next week.

Questions:
- What are the exact rollback SLAs and who is on-call? (answered: Redwood + BridgePoint contacts; runbook to follow)
- Will quantization require additional license or is it included? (answered: included in pilot; note potential memory/perf tradeoffs)
